rights_note: Reasoned US public-domain assessment based on New York publication in 1891. Internet Archive metadata supplies publication information but no explicit rights grant. Only factual construction text was used; no plates, image pixels, base meshes or textures were derived.
note: Catalog metadata and OCR text were actually read 2026-10-18; page/plate images have not been visually verified because archive storage redirects remain denied. OCR describes folded/stitched breast collar, breeching and girth, straight stitched 1-inch traces, flat reins, bridle with round check rein and plated front, nickel or Davis rubber trim. Component list and 25.4 mm trace-width conversion bound an original development harness only. Width is text-reported, not scan-verified attestation. All other dimensions, routes, fittings, colors and fit remain reconstructed. This is a light driving harness family, not riding equipment or a full collar/hames harness. No Chicago owner, 1835 use or particular horse is established.
what_it_supplies: An 1891 American commercial light-harness component recipe as OCR-read, pending original-page verification.
what_it_does_not_supply: Measured fit to the project horse or vehicle.
Proof this precise equipment was used by a named Chicago person or in 1835.
